openwrt_wiki.Einleitung: The Cudy TR3000 is a router designed for travel and portable use. It's powered with USB-C and features a USB3 port, Wi-Fi 6, and 1x2.5G WAN + 1x1G LAN port
openwrt_wiki.Hardware Highlights: The router has 3 WiFi antennas (two non-detachable external, and one internal). The internal antenna is for zero-wait DFS functionality only.
OEM easy installation: Determine the size of the flash on your device: 128 MB or 256 MB. You can find it on the carton or the label on your device (exact wording varies by market).

Download the Intermediate Firmware: https://www.cudy.com/blogs/faq/openwrt-software-download (Google Drive). ... Note that the 256 MB version has a separate firmware in the "TR3000 256 MB Flash V1 (Not for TR3000 V1)" folder. Wrong firmware will be rejected and will not brick your device.
If you are with 256 MB flash version and downloaded the 256 MB version, you already got the extracted version "cudy_tr3000-256mb-v1-sysupgrade.bin".

Enter the web interface at http://192.168.10.1/ with the default password "admin" (or the password you set during the initial setup of newer stock firmware). Go to "Upgrade Firmware" ... Wait 2 minutes.
Intermediate firmware: connect via Ethernet, LuCI at http://192.168.1.1/, then flash sysupgrade from firmware-selector.openwrt.org
openwrt_wiki.OpenWrt U-Boot layout: default available router space ~45 MB in the 128 MB version; OpenWrt U-Boot increases to 93 MB (nur 128-MB-Variante, Image cudy_tr3000-v1-ubootmod)
openwrt_wiki.Debricking: Cudy bootloader starts a TFTP client for OEM recovery using the Reset button, accepts only OEM firmware. Hard bricks: mtk_uartboot with mt7981-ram-ddr3-bl2.bin
openwrt_wiki.Flash Layout (128 MB): SLC SPI-NAND 128 MiB: BL2 1 MiB | u-boot-env 512 KiB | factory 2 MiB | bdinfo 256 KiB | FIP 2 MiB | ubi
openwrt_wiki.Opening the case: Remove the 4 rubber pads underneath (heat slightly), remove 4 Philips screws, bottom clipped to top with small tabs
openwrt_wiki.Serial / UART: On the bottom of the PCB you can find two small test points. If your PCB has the ethernet ports at left and the LEDs at right, then the left test point is RX and the right is TX. GND: any GND point on the board. Solder wires or use needles. 115200, 8N1, 3.3V
openwrt_wiki.Warnung: Cudy TR3000 request special tools for uart jumper as picture near end of the page.
